subject: Replace the nightly invoice export cron job with a queue-driven exporter

questions.question: Is the goal to stop missed exports, or to make exports near-real-time?
questions.recommended: Stop missed exports; real-time is a later, separate decision.
questions.answer: Stop missed exports. Finance only reads the file at 07:00.

questions.question: Who consumes the export file today?
questions.answer: Finance ops (3 people) via the shared drive; the ERP import job reads it at 06:30.
questions.source: export bucket access logs, last 90 days

questions.question: Must the file format stay byte-identical so the ERP import keeps working?
questions.recommended: Yes — keep the CSV schema frozen for this change.

questions.question: Is 'zero missed exports over 30 consecutive days' the success bar?
questions.recommended: Yes, 30 days with zero misses and alerting within 15 minutes of a failure.

questions.question: When the export fails twice, should the job page on-call or open a ticket for the morning?
questions.recommended: Page on-call before 05:30 so there is time to rerun before the 06:30 import.

questions.question: Do we keep the cron job runnable for two weeks as a fallback?
questions.recommended: Yes, disabled but deployable, removed after 14 clean days.

questions.question: Run old and new exporters in parallel for a week and diff the files before cutover?
questions.recommended: Yes — shadow-run for 7 nights, cut over after 7 identical diffs.

questions.question: Does the payments platform team own the exporter after cutover?
questions.recommended: Yes, it sits next to their invoicing service.

questions.question: Does the queue's retention cover a weekend outage?
questions.source: queue configuration in the infra repo

questions.question: Should the export later move to an API push into the ERP?
questions.recommended: Defer — out of this change; revisit after 30 clean days.
questions.reason: Needs ERP vendor input; not on the route to the goal.
